en: The biggest hackathon platform tells its winners: prize fulfillment can take up to sixty days from receipt of paperwork. And make sure your PayPal, Payoneer or Wise account is set up to receive dollars, or you may lose fees, or the prize.
This hackathon says the same thing in its own rules: winners may be required to set up a wallet address, plus acceptance documents and due diligence.
Every program that pays strangers runs this loop by hand. And the person whose paperwork was checked is never tied to the address that gets paid.

I'm on the receiving side. I'm a solo builder and engineering student in South Korea. I've entered about a dozen global hackathons since August, and my own money comes home through Paddle and Payoneer, with a hundred-dollar minimum and no payout in won.

The organizer locks every award on Tempo the day it announces winners, in one transaction. The winner opens their link once and touches their fingerprint. That passkey is their account: no app, no seed phrase, no gas.
When the organizer clears that winner's paperwork, the money lands in that exact account, in the same transaction. The paperwork and the payout are finally the same thing.
The winner gets a receipt in their own currency for their records, and can send the money on to an exchange, paying the tiny fee in the same dollars.

The rules live in the contract: nothing pays before clearance, a copied link can't redirect the money, a failed check is revoked and refunded, unclaimed awards come back. Every one of those refusals is a real transaction on Tempo testnet.
It's built on Tempo because each piece is a protocol feature there: transfer memos, native fee sponsorship, passkey accounts and batched calls.
Claim links are instant but ungated. Payout platforms are gated but need the winner to onboard. Claimdesk is both: a stranger with no wallet, paid only after paperwork.

Organizers pay half a percent per payout; winners pay nothing. We start with hackathons, bounties and grants, and the same flow pays contributors abroad, a market where Payoneer alone moved eighty-seven and a half billion dollars last year.
Next: one real program as a pilot, then mainnet with an identity and tax-form provider behind the clear button. Claimdesk: pay every winner by link.
